points.description: Names the property of spanning trees: there is a single unique path between every pair of nodes, so the tree has no loops while still reaching all nodes (equivalently, a loop-free subnet containing all nodes). This means no duplicate packets are sent. The student must state the unique-path or loop-free-and-spanning idea, not just say 'it is a tree'.
points.partial_credit: Half (0.25) for 'no loops' or 'connects all nodes' without the unique-path idea, or for 'a tree' with no explanation of why it suits broadcast/multicast.

points.description: Explains the modification to Link State Routing: multicast group membership is added to the link state packets so every node learns which nodes belong to which groups; once the full topology and group information reach every node, each node builds the multicast spanning tree locally from its complete state information (e.g. using Prim's or Kruskal's algorithm).
points.partial_credit: Half (0.25) if the student says group info is added to link state packets but not that each node computes the tree locally from the full topology, or vice versa.

rubric.notes: Full marks need both parts: the unique-path (loop-free, all-nodes) property for P1, and for P2 the idea that group membership is advertised in link state packets so each node can compute the spanning tree from the complete topology (Prim or Kruskal are examples, not required). Award half of a point for a partly stated idea, such as a vague mention of group information or a tree without the local computation. No marks for a generic answer such as 'spanning trees avoid loops' with no unique-path or loop-free idea, or for a modification that does not involve link state packets or group information.
